step1_analysis.description: A two-transistor sample-and-hold circuit used as a frame buffer pixel in LCOS microdisplays. It writes analog data to an intermediate storage capacitor (node N1) and later transfers it to the pixel electrode (node N0) to maximize image view time and brightness.

paper_reference.title: Novel Frame Buffer Pixel Circuits for Liquid-Crystal-on-Silicon Microdisplays

write_rise_time.description: Time required for the intermediate buffer node (N1) to charge from 10% to 90% of the DATA voltage during a write operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: R_on ≈ 1 / (u_n * C_ox * (W/L) * (V_GS - V_TH)). For W/L=10, V_GS=1.8V, V_DATA=1.0V, R_on ≈ 1kΩ. With C1=200fF, τ ≈ 200ps. Rise time (2.2τ) ≈ 440ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Depends on the transistor sizing and the buffer capacitance (200fF reported in paper).

read_rise_time.description: Time required for the pixel electrode (N0) to charge from 10% to 90% of its final value during a read operation.

sky130_expected.calculation: Similar to write, but driving C0=400fF from C1=200fF. τ ≈ 400ps. Rise time (2.2τ) ≈ 880ps.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Pixel capacitance is typically larger than buffer capacitance, leading to a slower time constant.

write_charge_injection.description: Voltage error introduced on the buffer node (N1) when the WRITE transistor turns off.

sky130_expected.calculation: ΔV = Q_ch / (2 * C1). Q_ch ≈ W*L*C_ox*(V_GS-V_TH) ≈ 2.5um² * 10fF/um² * 0.4V ≈ 10fC. ΔV ≈ 5fC / 200fF = 25mV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Charge injection is a primary source of error in sample-and-hold circuits, causing a slight voltage drop when the switch opens.

hold_voltage_drop.description: Voltage drop on the buffer node over a hold period due to subthreshold leakage and junction leakage.

sky130_expected.calculation: ΔV = I_leak * t_hold / C1. Assuming I_leak = 1pA, t_hold = 1.8us (in testbench), ΔV = 1pA * 1.8us / 200fF = 9uV.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The paper reports less than 1% drop over a full frame time (e.g., 180Hz = 5.5ms). In a short transient simulation, the drop will be very small.

step3_testbench.description: Transient analysis to measure write/read rise times, charge injection errors, and hold voltage drop in the frame buffer pixel.
step3_testbench.spice:
* Frame Buffer Pixel Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

.param W_xm1=5u L_xm1=0.5u
.param W_xm2=5u L_xm2=0.5u

* DUT
XM1 DATA WRITE N1 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm1} w={W_xm1}
XM2 N1 READ N0 GND sky130_fd_pr__nfet_01v8 l={L_xm2} w={W_xm2}

* Load Capacitors (from paper: 200fF buffer, 400fF pixel)
C1 N1 GND 200f
C0 N0 GND 400f

* Voltage Sources
VDD VDD GND 1.8
VDATA DATA GND 1.0

* Control Signals
* WRITE: High from 1us to 2us
VWRITE WRITE GND PULSE(0 1.8 1u 1n 1n 1u 10u)
* READ: High from 4us to 5us
VREAD READ GND PULSE(0 1.8 4u 1n 1n 1u 10u)

.control
tran 1n 6u

* Measure Write Rise Time (10% to 90% of 1.0V)
meas tran t_write_rise trig v(N1) val=0.1 rise=1 targ v(N1) val=0.9 rise=1

* Measure Write Charge Injection (Voltage drop when WRITE turns off)
meas tran v_n1_before_off find v(N1) at=1.99u
meas tran v_n1_after_off find v(N1) at=2.01u
let write_charge_inj = v_n1_before_off - v_n1_after_off
print write_charge_inj

* Measure Hold Voltage Drop (from 2.1us to 3.9us)
meas tran v_n1_hold_start find v(N1) at=2.1u
meas tran v_n1_hold_end find v(N1) at=3.9u
let hold_voltage_drop = v_n1_hold_start - v_n1_hold_end
print hold_voltage_drop

* Measure Read Rise Time (10% to 90% of expected 0.33V due to charge sharing between 200fF and 400fF)
meas tran t_read_rise trig v(N0) val=0.033 rise=1 targ v(N0) val=0.30 rise=1

quit
.endc
.end
